Be a Storyteller: Retell the story of the 'Four Friends' (Deer, Crow, Rat, Turtle) using your toys as actors! 🦌🐦🐁🐢
Number Names Challenge: How fast can you write the number names for 51 to 60 from your math book? ✍️
Phonics Hunt: Look around the room and find 3 things that start with 'cl', 'fl', or 'pl' blends. 🔍
Let's play 'Teacher'! Teach your parents the 'Lion and the Mouse' story you learned in Kannada class. �🐭
Shape Detectives: Find 3 things in your house that are spheres (like a ball) and 3 things that are cubes (like a box)! �⚽
Hindi Handwriting Hero: Practice writing your five favorite letters from the Nirjhar Moti book. �
Values Time: You learned about 'God is one'. Draw a beautiful picture showing everyone living together happily! �🖍️
Time Keepers: Look at the wall clock and tell your parents what time it is, just like you learned in Numeracy! ⏰
Vowel Catchers: Make a list of 5 words you know that have the long 'a' or 'i' sound (like cake or bike). 🅰️
Little Shopper: Use some pretend coins (or real ones!) and play 'Shop' like you learned in your Money chapter. �🛍️
Living or Non-Living?: Touch 5 things in your room and declare out loud if they are 'Living' or 'Non-Living'. 🌿🪨
Dictation Sprint: Have your parent give you a quick 5-word dictation test on 'r' blends (like crab, frog, green). �
Ascending Stairs: Arrange your toys or books from smallest to largest! �
Action Hero: Do the action for these words: jump, clap, smile, and sleep. Can your parent guess the action word? 🏃‍♂️
Kannada Numbers: Say the numbers 1 to 20 in Kannada as fast as you can! 🔢
Nature Saver: You learned 'Save our nature'. Find one way to save water or paper in your house today! 💧🌳
Data Detective: Group your toys by color and count which color has the most items, like a Pictograph! 📊
Opposites Game: Take turns with a parent saying opposites (Hot/Cold, Big/Small). See who runs out of words first! ⬆️⬇️
Rhyme Time: Sing your favorite school rhyme with all the actions! 🎶🙌
Sentence Builder: Write 2 simple sentences in your 4-line notebook using the naming words 'cat' and 'ball'. �
